primary_sources: MDN Web Responsive Design & Semantic HTML Standards

rules.rule_name: WCAG 2.1 Compliance and Semantic HTML HTML5 Markup
rules.explanation: Using generic non-semantic tags (e.g., clickable divs) breaks screen readers, keyboard navigation, and structural accessibility for users with disabilities.
rules.do: Use native HTML5 semantic tags (<main>, <nav>, <article>, <button>) and proper ARIA roles/labels when native elements are insufficient.
rules.dont: Do not attach click event listeners to un-focusable <div> or <span> elements without keyboard accessibility handlers and ARIA attributes.

rules.rule_name: Keyboard Navigation and Visual Focus States
rules.explanation: Removing default visual outline indicators prevents power users and visually impaired individuals from navigating the site using keyboard controls.
rules.do: Ensure all interactive controls receive logical tab focus order (tabindex) and display high-contrast visible focus rings when focused.
rules.dont: Do not apply CSS rules like `outline: none` or `outline: 0` without providing a distinct custom focus indicator.

rules.explanation: Hardcoding fixed pixel widths causes horizontal scrollbars, clipped text, and broken layouts across mobile and tablet viewports.
rules.do: Adopt mobile-first CSS media queries, fluid sizing units (rem, em, vw, %), and modern layout models (CSS Grid, Flexbox).
rules.dont: Do not use fixed pixel widths for main containers or rely on hardcoded magic layout offsets that break on varying screen sizes.

rules.rule_name: Design Token Consistency and Color Contrast Ratios
rules.explanation: Low contrast text renders content unreadable, while inconsistent ad-hoc styling breaks visual continuity across application modules.
rules.do: Enforce minimum color contrast ratios (4.5:1 for normal text per WCAG AA) and centralize design variables using CSS custom properties or design tokens.
rules.dont: Do not hardcode arbitrary hexadecimal color values or use low-contrast text against light background elements.
